event: Nala crosses to the apron and circles the pinned body wide, well clear of the fangs.

memory.fact: The dead wyrm hangs pinned on the spikes on the apron's east third, its tail a yard from the water.

event: It reeks of river mud and scorched flesh; flies are already settling on it.

memory.fact: The dead wyrm stinks of river mud and scorched flesh; flies gather on it within minutes.

event: She spins up a water disc and sets it to the thick neck; in about a minute it shears through.

memory.fact: A fast water disc took the dead wyrm's neck through in about a minute.
A fast water disc takes the dead wyrm's thick neck through in about a minute; an easy act.

event: The head rolls free on the stone, heavy as a sack of meal, fangs a hand long.

changes.note: The wyrm's head comes off on the weir apron, and there it lies

event: Jory and both barge crews come picking down the bank to the apron, and the miller unbars his door.
Nala cuts into the belly beside the spikes, working toward the liver for twenty minutes.

changes.note: Over twenty-five quiet minutes more mana returns than the disc spends

memory.fact: Opening the wyrm to reach its bile sac takes about twenty minutes of cutting.

event: The green sac lies whole beneath it. She ties off the duct with Mother Sallow's twine.

memory.fact: The Weir Wyrm's bile sac is a green bag the size of a fist, lying under its liver.
Nala's spikes passed a hand's breadth from the wyrm's bile sac; it lies whole under the liver.

event: Her blade slips on the slick flesh and nicks the sac; it bursts in her hands.

memory.fact: Nala found the wyrm's bile sac whole, but her blade slipped cutting it free; it burst, worthless.
Cutting a bile sac free whole is a moderate act; a burst sac is worthless, and its bile stings skin.

event: Bile sprays her wrists and forearms, and the skin there stings like nettles.

memory.fact: The burst wyrm bile stung Nala's wrists and forearms like nettles.

event: The jar stays empty. In the gut beside it lies a brass-buckled belt with a bowman's knife.

changes.note: Nala pulls Dickon's belt and knife from the wyrm's gut

memory.fact: The wyrm holds no crystal or pearl; Weir Wyrms grow none.

event: Jory goes quiet, staring at the belt in her hand. "That's Dickon's."

memory.fact: In the wyrm's gut lies a brass-buckled belt with a bowman's knife on it: Dickon's, Jory says.

event: He presses a gold coin into her stinging palm. "From both crews, like I said. You earned it."

changes.note: Jory pays the barge crews' promised gold, 100 copper

memory.fact: Jory and both crews come down to the apron, and Jory pays Nala the crews' gold at once.

event: Tam Hobb, stout and grey, eyes the head. "Eighty pound if it's an ounce. A long haul to town."

memory.fact: Miller Tam Hobb is a stout, grey man in a flour-dusted apron.
The wyrm's head weighs about 80 pounds, a heavy load to carry two hours without help.

event: "Take my mill barrow. Send it back on any barge coming down; I mean to grind by afternoon."

memory.fact: Tam Hobb unbars at the thunder and lends Nala his mill barrow to wheel the head to Wendlow.
Tam asks the barrow back by any barge coming down from Wendlow; he means to grind by afternoon.
Wheeling the 80-pound head in the barrow, the towpath to Wendlow takes about two and a half hours.

event: "Eh, thanks, but they said the fangs would be enough," Nala tells Tam.

memory.fact: Tam Hobb shrugs off the refused barrow and offers Nala a loaf and a cup of ale for the road.

event: "Just cut off the head to make sure it was dead."

memory.fact: Nala left the Weir Wyrm's head on the weir apron with its carcass.

event: She spins up a water blade and works it around the jaw; both fangs come free clean and whole.

changes.note: A water blade at the jaw spends 10 mana

memory.fact: Two fangs, each a hand long and about a pound, come from the wyrm's jaw with a water blade; easy.

event: Each is a hand long, hooked and yellow-white. She wraps them and stows them in her pack.

changes.note: Nala cuts the wyrm's two fangs free and stows them in her pack

memory.fact: Nala cut the wyrm's two fangs out whole: hooked, yellow-white, each a hand long.
Nala wrapped the Weir Wyrm's two fangs in a scrap of cloth and carries them in her pack.

event: She draws water and fire together into a gentle steam and plays it over her skin and clothes.

memory.fact: Water and fire woven make steam; air and fire woven make a hot, drying wind.
A gentle steam weave played over her own skin and clothes cleans them without scalding; no roll.

event: Bile, blood and river muck roll off her in a hot cloud; the sting in her forearms eases.

memory.fact: Steam washes the wyrm bile off Nala's arms, and the nettle sting fades within the hour.

event: Then air and fire: a hot wind wraps her for three minutes and leaves her dry.

changes.note: Steam and hot wind cost more than the few minutes give back

memory.fact: Nala's water-and-fire steam washes her clean; an air-and-fire wind dries her in three minutes.
A steam clean or a hot-wind dry costs 10 mana a minute; each takes about three minutes.

event: Tam Hobb snorts, half a laugh. "Handy trick. I'll be grinding by two, then."

changes.note: The miller and barge crews watch her work steam and wind

memory.fact: Seeing Nala steam herself clean, Tam Hobb calls it a handy trick and says he'll be grinding by two.

event: The crews whistle and start back up the bank toward their barges.

memory.fact: Once Nala has the fangs, the barge crews whistle and head back up the bank to their barges.

event: Jory lingers, eyes on Dickon's belt in Nala's hand, and slowly holds out his own.

memory.fact: Jory lingers, eyes on Dickon's belt in Nala's hand, and slowly holds out his own hand.
Jory eyes Dickon's belt in her hand and asks for it, to take to Dickon's mother at Brennock Ford.

event: Nala hands Dickon's belt to Jory.

changes.note: Nala hands Dickon's belt to Jory at the weir
Dickon's belt stays with Jory at Hobb's weir

event: He takes it with a bow of the head. "I'll carry it to his mother at Brennock Ford."

memory.fact: Jory takes Dickon's belt with a bow of the head; he'll carry it to Dickon's mother at Brennock Ford.

event: "The Wend Maid owes you passage anywhere on the Wend, any time. Free."

memory.fact: Jory tells Nala the Wend Maid owes her passage anywhere on the Wend, any time, free.

event: Nala takes the towpath back north under the willows; the walk passes quietly.

memory.fact: The towpath back from Hobb's Mill passes quietly on day 8.
A flat towpath runs the Wend's east bank from Wendlow to Hobb's Mill, under willows.

event: A little before half past two she reaches Wendlow's gate, mouth dry from the road.

changes.note: Two hours' walk fills her mana again

memory.fact: The walk back from Hobb's Mill brings Nala to Wendlow's gate a little before 14:30.

event: The watch knows her now. She pays her copper and is waved through with a grin.

changes.note: Wendlow's gate toll, one copper

memory.fact: At the gate the watch knows her now; she pays her copper and is waved through with a grin.

event: At Antler Hall she unwraps the two hooked, yellow-white fangs on the counter.
Grete turns one over. "Eighty pounds of head is too much to haul. These will do."

memory.fact: Grete counts an 80-pound wyrm head too big to carry; she pays the Weir Wyrm's bounty on its fangs.

event: "Box is empty since your last lot," she says, and writes a chit for fifteen gold.

memory.fact: The Board's strongbox is empty since Nala's payout; for the wyrm Grete writes a 15-gold chit.
Nala turned in the Weir Wyrm's fangs at Antler Hall; she carries Grete's signed 15-gold chit.

event: "Paid with the other when the tax rider comes tomorrow." She signs it and slides it over.

memory.fact: The wyrm's 15-gold chit is paid with the other from the magistrate's purse when the tax rider comes.

event: She hangs the fangs on a nail beside Voss's head and wipes the Weir Wyrm off the Board.

changes.note: Nala turns the wyrm's fangs in at Antler Hall
Grete hangs the fangs on a nail in Antler Hall

memory.fact: Grete hangs the wyrm's fangs on a nail beside Voss's head and wipes the wyrm off the Board.

event: "That letter went to the magistrate yesterday," she adds, low. "That's all I'll say of it."

memory.fact: Asked nothing, Grete says only that the letter went to the magistrate yesterday, and no more of it.

event: "Board's bare till the rider brings fresh slips tomorrow," Grete says, and dips her pen in the ink.

memory.fact: Grete says the Board is bare till the rider brings fresh slips, and dips her pen in the ink.
No new contract is posted on day 8; Grete expects fresh slips with the tax rider on day 9.

event: Nala finds a quiet spot and lays out her wool tunic: a bolt-torn rent at the ribs, a slit sleeve.

memory.fact: Nala's wool tunic has a bolt-torn rent at the left ribs and a slit sleeve; her cloak hem is ragged.

event: Her cloak hem hangs ragged too.
She starts with the pairs she knows. Fire scorches a brown edge onto the rent; she snuffs it fast.

changes.note: A fingertip of fire on the cloth spends 10 mana

memory.fact: Testing fire on it left a scorched brown border by the felted seam at Nala's tunic ribs.

event: Air frays the threads looser. Water alone only soaks the cloth.

memory.fact: Trying weaves on cloth, fire scorches it, air frays it, and water alone only wets it.

event: She tries pair after pair through the warm afternoon, and the tunic takes each one badly.

memory.fact: On wool, fire with air singes, air with water wets and fluffs, and fire with earth stiffens it.
Finding the felting weave by trial takes about two hours, needs no roll, and is a Weave use.

event: Earth with water, last: the wool fibres creep together and lock.

memory.fact: An earth-and-water weave worked into a wool tear felts its fibres shut in a stiff, ridged seam.
Earth and water woven bind as one working, felt as a heavy, wet pull behind her breastbone.

event: The rent at the ribs felts shut in a stiff, ridged seam, a hand-span long, in about five minutes.

changes.note: An afternoon of trial weaves and the rib felting spend her mana

memory.fact: Felting a hand-span wool tear shut takes Nala about five minutes.
Felting wool costs 10 mana a minute; a hand-span tear takes about five minutes, with no roll.

event: She works the slit sleeve the same way; another ridge, stiff but whole.

changes.note: Felting the slit sleeve spends more mana than returns meanwhile

event: Throat dry from the long afternoon, Nala pulls the tunic on and rolls her shoulders; the seams hold.

memory.fact: On day 8 Nala felted her tunic's rib rent and slit sleeve shut; it is whole, stiff at the seams.

event: At the Bell and Barrel, supper is eel stew, black bread and small beer; eight copper with the bed.

changes.note: Bram takes 8 copper for supper and the bed

memory.fact: Bell and Barrel supper on day 8 is eel stew, black bread and small beer.
On day 8 Bram Cooley took 8 copper for Nala's eel-stew supper and bed together.

event: Nell Cooley eyes Nala's ragged cloak hem. "I stitch tears, two copper apiece. Say the word."

memory.fact: At supper Nell Cooley eyes Nala's ragged cloak hem and offers to stitch it, 2 copper a tear.
Nell Cooley at the Bell and Barrel mends torn clothes with needle and thread, 2 copper a tear.

event: The taproom is loud: bargemen toast the Weir Wyrm's death. The river is open again.

memory.fact: That evening bargemen in the taproom toast the Weir Wyrm's death; the river is open again.

event: Word has caught up: the Wyrm's killer is the woman who ended Voss. Heads turn; some stare.

memory.fact: The taproom now knows the wyrm's killer is the same woman who ended Voss; some stare at Nala.

event: Nala sleeps behind a bolted door, and wakes rested at first light on day nine.

changes.note: A night's sleep fills her mana

memory.fact: Nala's night of day 8 at the Bell and Barrel passes quietly; she wakes rested about 6:00 on day 9.

event: Porridge with honey and small beer, two copper, then up the high street to Antler Hall.

changes.note: Porridge and small beer, 2 copper

memory.fact: Breakfast on day 9 is the Bell and Barrel's porridge with honey and small beer.
Bell and Barrel breakfast is porridge with honey and small beer, worth 2 copper.

event: Grete waves her to a bench. "Rider's due mid-morning. Sit."
Near ten, hooves on the high street: the tax rider and four guards, with the magistrate's purse.

memory.fact: The tax rider rides in about 10:00 on day 9 with four guards and the magistrate's purse.

event: By half past ten the Board's share is on Grete's counter. She counts out twenty-six gold.

changes.note: Grete pays both chits, 26 gold

memory.fact: By 10:30 on day 9 the Board's share reaches Antler Hall; Grete pays both of Nala's chits, 26 gold.

event: "Both chits, paid." She tears them across and drops the halves in a box.
She pins two new slips to the Board beside the reeve's old one.

memory.fact: The rider brings two slips; the reeve's 8 gold for why Greyfen crystals went dark still stands too.

event: "Eighteen gold: a mantis-beast, Level 20, taking sheep and a shepherd on Coldbrook Downs."

memory.fact: New slip: 18 gold for a Level 20 mantis-beast taking sheep and a shepherd on Coldbrook Downs.

event: "A day's walk north. Pays on its head or its forelimbs."

memory.fact: Coldbrook Downs lie a day's walk north of Wendlow; the mantis bounty pays on its head or forelimbs.

event: "Twelve gold: Cal Ferrin, the Ferryman, Level 16, robbing folk at Lowcross ferry. Alive or dead."

memory.fact: New slip: 12 gold for Cal Ferrin, the Ferryman, a Level 16 outlaw robbing folk at Lowcross ferry.

event: "Half a day east. And the reeve's eight for the Greyfen crystals still stands."

memory.fact: Lowcross ferry lies half a day east of Wendlow; the Ferryman's bounty pays on him, alive or dead.

event: Grete unfolds a note that came with the purse, reads it, and holds it out to Nala.
"Magistrate Varne asks Nala Arthur to the Moot Hall at noon. Mind your tongue up there."

changes.note: Grete hands Nala the magistrate's note

memory.fact: With the Board's share comes a note: Magistrate Varne asks Nala Arthur to the Moot Hall at noon.
Grete reads the magistrate's note, says only 'Mind your tongue up there,' and hands it over.

event: Nala tucks the magistrate's note into her pack and takes her leave of Antler Hall.
Down the high street to the Bell and Barrel; the taproom is near empty, the fire ticking.
Nala takes the bench by the hearth and spreads the cloak over her knees, hem to the light.
Brambles have chewed the hem through in three places, the worst at the back where rock tore it.
The rest of the wool is sound, and the tunic's felted seams still hold from yesterday.
She takes the hem between her fingers and sets the earth-and-water weave into the first tear.
The wet pull settles behind her breastbone; the chewed strands creep together and lock.
The tear shuts in a stiff, dark ridge, like the ones along her tunic.
She works on to the second place and the third, her well draining steadily the whole time.
The last ravel felts shut, her well near half spent; the hem hangs whole, ridged and dark.

changes.note: Cloak hem felted shut in three stiff dark ridges
changes.from: A hooded cloak of heavy grey-green wool, fastened with a wooden toggle, its hem hanging ragged, chewed by brambles and rock.
changes.to: A hooded cloak of heavy grey-green wool, fastened with a wooden toggle. The hem, chewed through in three places by brambles and rock, the worst at the back, is felted shut in stiff, dark ridges; the rest of the wool is sound.

changes.note: 20 minutes of felting spend 200 mana; two ten-minute returns give back 72: 232

memory.fact: On day 9 Nala felted her cloak's chewed hem shut in three stiff, dark ridges.
On day 9 Nala felted her cloak's chewed hem shut in three stiff, dark ridges.
On day 9 Nala felted her cloak's chewed hem shut in three stiff, dark ridges.

event: She shakes the cloak out and looks over the rest of her clothes.
The leggings are sound, and the grey shirt and black tights from Earth take no weave at all.

memory.fact: Alan's Earth-made clothes answer no Starfall weave; the grey shirt and black tights take no mend.
Alan's Earth-made clothes answer no Starfall weave; the grey shirt and black tights take no mend.

event: Her boots are leather and want no mending; Nala pulls the cloak on and rolls her shoulders.
She crosses the square to the Moot Hall, grey stone with its door up a broad flight of steps.

memory.fact: The Moot Hall stands on the square, a grey stone hall with its door up a broad flight of steps.
The Moot Hall stands on the square, a grey stone hall with its door up a broad flight of steps.
Odile Varne holds her court in the Moot Hall, the town hall on the square.
Odile Varne holds her court in the Moot Hall, the town hall on the square.

event: Two watchmen at the door look at her sword, then at her antler badge, and let her by.

memory.fact: Two watchmen keep the Moot Hall's door, and let a hunter in with her sword.
Two watchmen keep the Moot Hall's door, and let a hunter in with her sword.

event: Inside, a thin clerk at a desk reads the seal on her note and writes her in his book.

memory.fact: Her court sits at noon; the town clerk writes each name at the door and calls them in that order.
Her court sits at noon; the town clerk writes each name at the door and calls them in that order.

event: She takes a bench at the side among the morning's other business: a drover, a hen-woman.
The square bell rings twelve; the clerk takes up his book and the room goes quiet.
The Moot Hall is one long room: a raised bench, the clerk's desk, and presses of tax rolls.

memory.fact: Inside is one long room: a raised bench, the clerk's desk below it, and presses of tax rolls.
Inside is one long room: a raised bench, the clerk's desk below it, and presses of tax rolls.

event: Behind the bench sits a thin, silver-haired woman in grey velvet, ink on her fingers.

memory.fact: She is thin and silver-haired, with ink-stained fingers and a grey velvet coat.
She is thin and silver-haired, with ink-stained fingers and a grey velvet coat.

event: The drover's boundary quarrel is heard and settled fast; the hen-woman is sent to the watch.
The clerk calls "Nala Arthur," and she comes forward to stand before the bench.
The clerk names her judge: Odile Varne, Magistrate of Wendlow, who sits for the margrave.

memory.fact: Odile Varne, Magistrate of Wendlow, sits in judgement for the margrave.
Odile Varne, Magistrate of Wendlow, sits in judgement for the margrave.
Odile Varne, Magistrate of Wendlow, sits in judgement for the margrave.

event: On the bench before the magistrate lies a folded sheet, its red wax seal broken open.
"Grete Holm sent me this the day it came off the quarry road," Varne says, "with no word."

memory.fact: Grete Holm sent Odile Varne the letter the day it came off the quarry road, with no word.
Grete Holm sent Odile Varne the letter the day it came off the quarry road, with no word.
Grete Holm sent Odile Varne the letter the day it came off the quarry road, with no word.
Grete Holm sent Odile Varne the letter the day it came off the quarry road, with no word.

event: "The seal on it is the merchants' counting-house's, and Harl Voss kept no such company."

memory.fact: Odile Varne says Harl Voss kept no company with the merchants' counting-house.
Odile Varne says Harl Voss kept no company with the merchants' counting-house.
Odile Varne says Harl Voss kept no company with the merchants' counting-house.
Odile Varne says Harl Voss kept no company with the merchants' counting-house.

event: She opens the sheet flat with two inked fingers and leaves it lying between them.
"So," says Odile Varne, "who else has read what is written here?"

changes.note: An hour's return, 36 each ten minutes, fills her mana to 360
Mana 360 at the turn's end

memory.fact: Odile Varne wants to learn whether Nala read Voss's letter, and who else she has told of it.
Odile Varne wants to learn whether Nala read Voss's letter, and who else she has told of it.

memory.fact: Nala told Varne only she and Grete know of Voss's letter, and that she never looked inside it.
Nala told Varne only she and Grete know of Voss's letter, and that she never looked inside it.
Nala told Varne only she and Grete know of Voss's letter, and that she never looked inside it.
Nala told Varne only she and Grete know of Voss's letter, and that she never looked inside it.

event: Varne's eyes rest on Nala's face a long moment, as if listening for something under the words.
Then her shoulders ease a fraction, and she nods once, as if a sum has come out even.
She folds the sheet along its creases and lays it in a press behind the bench, then turns the key.

memory.fact: Varne locked Voss's letter in a press behind her bench in the Moot Hall.
Varne locked Voss's letter in a press behind her bench in the Moot Hall.
Varne locked Voss's letter in a press behind her bench in the Moot Hall.
Varne locked Voss's letter in a press behind her bench in the Moot Hall.

Varne bound Nala to keep Voss's letter between the three of them; Grete knows to hold her tongue.
Varne bound Nala to keep Voss's letter between the three of them; Grete knows to hold her tongue.
Varne bound Nala to keep Voss's letter between the three of them; Grete knows to hold her tongue.

event: She lays her inked hands flat on the bench. "A hunter who can keep quiet is worth something to me."
"A stranger with no lord and no papers gets asked about in my town, sooner or later."

memory.fact: Varne says a stranger with no lord and no papers gets asked about in Wendlow, sooner or later.
Varne says a stranger with no lord and no papers gets asked about in Wendlow, sooner or later.
Varne says a stranger with no lord and no papers gets asked about in Wendlow, sooner or later.
Varne says a stranger with no lord and no papers gets asked about in Wendlow, sooner or later.

For Nala's silence, Varne offers her papers as a sworn hunter of Wendlow, under Varne's seal.
For Nala's silence, Varne offers her papers as a sworn hunter of Wendlow, under Varne's seal.
For Nala's silence, Varne offers her papers as a sworn hunter of Wendlow, under Varne's seal.

event: "Papers like that answer any gate, any reeve, any watch that asks who you are."

Varne says papers under her seal answer any gate, reeve or watch that asks who the bearer is.

Varne names what the papers need: "Your home, and your lord, to write on them."

Varne asks Nala her home and her lord, to write on her papers.

Nala told Varne she was born in the wilds, with no home, no lord and no papers.

"Wendlow will do." She writes. "Home, Wendlow. Lord, the margrave, served through this bench."

Nala's papers name her home Wendlow and her lord the margrave, served through Varne's bench.

A sworn hunter of Wendlow answers Varne's bench against outlaws and beasts, paid at Board rates.
A sworn hunter of Wendlow answers Varne's bench against outlaws and beasts, paid at Board rates.
